matched_finding.description: The analysis plan describes two mutually contradictory rules for classifying discussed items. First, the authors establish a nuanced rule: if a partner happens to provide an answer consistent with what the participant saw (e.g., correctly guessing 'white mug'), the discussion item will NOT be classified as containing misinformation. This is methodologically sensible. However, immediately after, a blanket rule is stated: 'we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner's differing version.' These two rules are logically incompatible. The blanket categorization would inflate apparent misinformation exposure and misclassify some control-condition-like trials as misinformation trials, biasing the primary within-subjects comparison.
matched_finding.quote: 'However, if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen, that is, "white mug"...the situation will not be classified as misleading.' Versus: 'In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation.'

matched_finding.description: The manuscript contains a direct self-contradiction about when the interventions are administered. In one passage of the introduction the authors explicitly state they chose to place the warning after the collaborative recall. In a later passage of the same introduction they state the opposite—that interventions are placed before collaborative recall—and give a rationale for this. The actual procedure described in Section 2.5 lists the phase order as: (1) movie, (2) collaborative recall, (3) intervention, (4) individual memory test, placing interventions after collaborative recall. This means the theoretical rationale offered for pre-exposure inoculation ('we wanted to inoculate participants against the influence of misinformation before it could take effect') does not match the actual procedure, undermining the theoretical framing of the study.
matched_finding.quote: 'In the present study we decided to place the warning after the collaborative recall (see the rationale for the research below).' Versus: 'What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation).' Versus procedure: '(1) presenting the original material, (2) collaborative recall (including misinformation), (3) three procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation...and (4) an individual memory test.'

matched_finding.description: The authors conclude that normative social influence is 'completely ruled out' because the individual memory test involves no interpersonal pressure. This reasoning conflates the moment of influence with the moment of expression. Normative influence during the discussion phase could cause participants to publicly agree with their partner, and this public compliance could then produce memory updating (source monitoring confusion about whether the partner's version is now their own recollection), which is then expressed in the individual test. Ruling out normative influence at the test stage does not rule out normative influence at the encoding/discussion stage. This premature dismissal is consequential because the interventions are then theorized exclusively around informational influence mechanisms, potentially missing an important process the interventions could also target or be undermined by.
matched_finding.quote: 'Given the fact that the individual memory test does not include any element of direct interpersonal pressure, we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is no cost of disagreeing.'

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Open-ended→forced-choice changes baseline conformity rate and scoring categories — must know format matters
ground_truth.original_snippet: In the present research, the individual memory test will be in the form of open-ended questions.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.
ground_truth.description: Changed from open-ended to forced-choice — inflates conformity rates (50% guessing baseline vs much lower); scoring categories (correct, misinformation, other) don't make sense with forced-choice

matched_finding.description: The procedure section explicitly states that the individual memory test uses open-ended questions, and the opening of the analysis plan confirms this as a deliberate methodological departure from prior work. However, later in the same analysis plan section the authors write that 'the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format,' directly contradicting the stated design. These two formats have fundamentally different psychometric properties, scoring procedures, response bias profiles, and comparability to prior MORI-technique studies. The contradiction makes it impossible to evaluate the study's measurement approach, and means one section of the manuscript must be incorrect.
matched_finding.quote: Procedure (Section 2.5): 'The test will contain 20 open-ended questions, eight of which will cover all the critical details.' Analysis plan (Section 3): 'First we will examine the memory conformity effect...but with modification concerning applying open-ended questions.' Then later in Section 3: 'In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.'

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Co-witness exposure exclusion removed — must know non-exposed participants dilute the effect
ground_truth.original_snippet: In addition, participants who are not exposed to co-witness details at all (that is, the participants who did not hear any potentially misleading information from the partner) will be excluded from the analyses.
ground_truth.description: Removed exclusion of non-exposed participants — including those who received zero misinformation dilutes the conformity effect and biases against finding both the basic effect and intervention benefit
